lectures.title: SC/ST rights: safeguards, laws, commissions, judgements and schemes

parts.t: Constitutional provisions for SCs and STs
items: Special provisions for SCs, STs, OBCs
**First Constitutional Provision against Untouchability (abolishing untouchability):** Article 17.
**First Constitutional Safeguard for SCs & STs:** Articles 15(4) and 16(4).
**First Reservation Policy in India:** Kolhapur State (1902).
**First State to Implement Reservation:** Kolhapur State under Shahu Maharaj.
**First Ruler to Introduce Reservation:** Shahu Maharaj.

parts.t: National Commissions and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
items: **First National Commission for Scheduled Castes:** under Article 338; constitutional status under the 65th Amendment.
**First Separate National Commission for SCs (National Commission for Scheduled Castes):** 2004.
**First Separate National Commission for STs (National Commission for Scheduled Tribes):** 2004.
**First Ministry exclusively for Tribal Affairs:** Ministry of Tribal Affairs (1999); in 1999 Tribal Affairs functions were separated to create the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
**Ministry of Tribal Affairs deals with:** Scheduled Tribes; PESA implementation; Forest Rights Act; Tribal education and development.

parts.t: Laws against untouchability, atrocities and manual scavenging
items: **Caste Disabilities Removal Act (1850):** Removed legal disabilities due to caste conversion.
**Enforcement:** June 1, 1955; renamed in 1976 from the Untouchability Offences Act.
**Purpose:** Enforces Article 17; punishes the practice of untouchability; prescribes penalties for enforcing religious and social disabilities arising from untouchability.
SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
**Size and enforcement:** 23 sections; enforced 30 January 1990 (effective 1990); amended August 20, 2018 (Amendment Act, 2018).
**Purpose:** Prevents atrocities against SCs/STs (protection from atrocities); explicit list of atrocities; no anticipatory bail.
**Section 18A:** bars anticipatory bail and removes the requirement of preliminary inquiry or prior sanction before arrest.
**Acts compared (Social/Security Acts):** SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989; PWDVA, 2005 (effective 2006); MISA, 1971 was an internal security statute, not a social welfare act.
Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013
**Provisions:** Complete prohibition of hazardous manual cleaning of sewer/septic tanks; mandates mechanization and alternative livelihood rehabilitation.
**Ban:** Total ban on manual cleaning of unsanitary latrines, open drains, and sewers without protective gear.
**Key initiatives:** Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955; SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2018; National Toll-Free Helpline (14566).
**Mechanism:** Automatic FIR registration without preliminary inquiry; central assistance for atrocity victim relief and inter-caste marriage incentives.

parts.t: Tribal laws: PESA and the Forest Rights Act
items: **Provisions:** Extends Part IX of the Constitution to Schedule V areas, empowering traditional Gram Sabhas.
**Gram Sabha authority:** over natural resources, minor forest produce, dispute resolution, and project approvals in Schedule V areas.
**Enforcement:** December 31, 2007 (Rules notified: Jan 1, 2008). Recognizes tribal forest rights.
**Provisions:** Recognizes (vests) individual and community forest rights (IFR/CFR) in forest-dwelling STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (OTFD).
Formulated the classic 5 criteria for ST scheduling
Dilip Singh Bhuria; Ministry of Rural Development
Prof. Virginius Xaxa; Prime Minister’s Office (PMO)
**Lokur Committee's 5 criteria for ST scheduling:** primitive traits, distinct culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact, and backwardness.
**Bhuria Committee:** recommended constitutional recognition of traditional Gram Sabhas in Schedule V areas.

**Xaxa Committee:** Comprehensive evaluation of socio-economic, health, and educational status of tribal communities; recommended preventing tribal land alienation and strictly enforcing the FRA, 2006.
**Justice K.G. Balakrishnan Commission:** Examining the legal feasibility of according SC status to Dalits who converted to religions other than Hinduism, Sikhism, and Buddhism.
**Rajiv Gauba Committee:** Formed to explore equitable administrative mechanisms and alternative interventions for the most backward sub-castes among SCs (e.g., Madigas).

**M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006):** Upheld (validated) reservation in promotions for SC/STs subject to quantifiable data demonstrating backwardness, inadequate representation, and overall administrative efficiency (Art. 335).
**Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018):** Removed the requirement to prove backwardness for SC/STs in promotions; extended the creamy layer principle to SC/ST promotions.

**State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024):** 7-judge bench overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004); affirmed states have constitutional power under Arts. 15(4) & 16(4) to sub-classify SCs/STs using empirical data.
**Davinder Singh (2024) also:** recommended creamy layer identification.
**Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997):** Nullified mining leases to non-tribals in Schedule V areas; held that tribal land cannot be leased to private parties or corporations.
**Orissa Mining Corp. v. MoEF (Niyamgiri Case, 2013):** Affirmed statutory role of the Gram Sabha under FRA 2006 to safeguard religious and cultural rights of Dongria Kondh tribals.
Village development, socio-economic infrastructure, and hostels
Mechanized sanitation ecosystems, zero manual scavenging deaths, rehabilitation of sanitation workers
Residential education in top private schools for meritorious SC students
**PM-AJAY merges:** Adarsh Gram, SCA to SCSP, and Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana.
Saturation of 11 critical interventions for 75 PVTG communities
Comprehensive saturation of basic infrastructure across ~63,000 tribal-majority villages
Quality middle/high school education for tribal students in remote areas
Target to eliminate Sickle Cell Anaemia by 2047
**PM-JANMAN's 11 critical interventions include:** housing, roads, clean water, electrification.
**National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission:** focusing heavily on screening tribal populations.
End-to-end planning, fund convergence, and monitoring of SC-majority Adarsh Gram infrastructure works
Digital profiling, health insurance linkage, and PPE verification for sewer/septic tank workers
Online CBT registration, merit evaluation, and seat allotment in private residential schools for SC students
Inter-ministerial saturation dashboard for 11 critical interventions across 75 PVTG communities
Central registry tracking Sickle Cell trait/disease screening cards for tribal populations
Dedicated e-commerce gateway connecting tribal artisans and forest-produce collectors directly to buyers
**Caste Discrimination & Atrocities: NGRS / National Helpline for Prevention of Atrocities (14566):** Social Justice & Empowerment (DoSJE).
**Helpline 14566:** 24/7 web-linked toll-free helpline providing immediate grievance escalation under the POA and PCR Acts.

lectures.title: Child rights: constitutional protection, laws, bodies, judgements and schemes

items: Prohibition of Child Labour (Child Labour prohibited)
**Education (constitutional provisions):** Article 21A; Right to Education Act, 2009.

parts.t: Firsts: policy, bodies, convention and helpline
items: **First International Convention on Child Rights Ratified by India:** United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, UNCRC (1992).
**First National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR):** 2007.
**First Juvenile Justice Law:** Juvenile Justice Act, 1986.
**First (comprehensive) Child Marriage Restraint Law:** Child Marriage Restraint Act (Sharda Act), 1929.
**Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA), 2006:** enforced November 1, 2007; replaced the 1929 Sarda Act; prevents child marriage.
**PCMA provisions:** Defines (fixes) marriageable / minimum age at 18 for females and 21 for males; child marriages are voidable at the child's option.

parts.t: Child labour: laws, committee and enforcement
items: **First Child Labour Law in India:** Children (Pledging of Labour) Act, 1933 (Children Act, 1933).
**First Comprehensive Child Labour Law:** Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (Child Labour Act, 1986).
**Gurupadaswamy Committee (1979), Ministry of Labour:** Landmark committee that recognized child labour is directly tied to poverty; led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.
**Gurupadaswamy Committee recommended:** a dual approach of banning hazardous child labor while regulating other forms.
**Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986:** enforced December 23, 1986; Major Amendment: Sept 1, 2016 (Amended 2016).
**Provisions:** Complete ban (prohibition) on employing children below 14 in all occupations; regulates (restricts) adolescents (14–18) working in hazardous conditions / processes.
**PENCIL Portal (Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour):** Labour & Employment (MoLE); for Child Labour & Exploitation.
**PENCIL mechanism:** Inter-agency tracking (coordination) mechanism linking Child Labour Committees, police, and NGOs to rescue and rehabilitate (rehab) child labourers.
**First Constitutional Amendment making Education a Fundamental Right:** 86th Amendment, 2002.
**Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009:** enforced April 1, 2010; universal elementary education.
**RTE provisions:** Enforces Article 21A; free and compulsory education (ages 6–14); mandates 25% reservation (quota) for disadvantaged groups in private unaided schools.

parts.t: Child protection laws: CPCR, POCSO and Juvenile Justice
items: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act, 2005
**Provisions:** Established (constituted) NCPCR and SCPCRs as statutory bodies (statutory watchdogs) for children's legal and constitutional rights and child welfare monitoring.
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012
**Provisions:** Gender-neutral law punishing child sexual abuse; stringent punishments; child-friendly special courts; mandatory reporting.
**2019 amendment:** added capital punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
**Enforcement:** January 15, 2016; amended by the 2021 amendment, in force Sept 1, 2022.
**Provisions:** Permits (allows) trial of juveniles aged 16–18 as adults for heinous offenses (crimes).
**2021/2022 amendment:** DMs/ADMs (District Magistrates) empowered to issue adoption orders, for accelerated adoption orders.
**Child Labour & Abuse, key initiatives:** PENCIL Portal; POCSO Amendment Act (Stringent punishments); Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Act.

parts.t: Committee on child protection and adoption
items: **Justice Deepak Verma Committee (Supreme Court of India / WCD):** Framed guidelines streamlining adoption processes and oversight on childcare institutions (CCIs) under the Juvenile Justice framework.

parts.t: Landmark judgements on child protection and labour
items: **M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996):** Banned child labour in hazardous industries; mandated establishment of a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund.
**Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011):** Issued guidelines against trafficking, child begging, and circus child labor; mandated human-rights oversight of all Child Care Institutions.

**Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017):** Struck down the marital rape exception for minor wives under IPC Section 375; intercourse with a girl below 18 is statutory rape, regardless of marriage.
**Mission Vatsalya (Women & Child Development):** Child protection, foster care, institutional juvenile justice homes, and emergency helpline (Childline 1098 integrated with 112).
**Mission Saksham Anganwadi & POSHAN 2.0 (Women & Child Development):** Poshan Tracker, Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi (ECCE), and tech-driven nutrition monitoring for 0–6 age group.
Real-time digital tracking of Anganwadi service delivery, stunting/wasting, and nutrition metrics (0–6 years)
Centralized database tracking missing, vulnerable, and institutionalized children under Mission Vatsalya
Online platform ensuring transparent, non-discretionary child adoption referrals and status tracking
Child Abuse (Sexual / Cyber): confidential, direct digital reporting window
**POCSO E-Box:** for children and guardians to report online and physical sexual abuse.
**Target group of these platforms:** Children & Infants.
